cards.explanation: The answer is False. The four angels are holding back the winds "…so that no wind would blow on land or sea or on any tree." (Revelation 7:1) That means no breeze at all, not even a tiny one. A leaf up there wouldn't get to wiggle, friends.

The answer is True. John says he saw another angel ascending from the east, "…with the seal of the living God." (Revelation 7:2) The angel isn't carrying just any seal. It belongs to the living God. I know a little about seals, friends, since I'm a stamper, but this one is in a whole different league.

The answer is to harm the land and the sea. John says the four angels "…had been given power to harm the land and the sea…" (Revelation 7:2) So the angel from the east is calling out to the ones holding that power. A loud voice for a big moment, friends, and I'd say he had everybody's attention.

The answer is that God's servants get sealed. The angel says, "Do not harm the land or sea or trees until we have placed a seal on the foreheads of the servants of our God." (Revelation 7:3) So the sealing comes first, friends.

The answer is Israel. John hears the number: "…144,000 from all the tribes of Israel…" (Revelation 7:4) Then he hears the tribes listed one by one. It's quite a list, friends, and I'm still working on remembering my own six cookie cutter kids' toppings.

The answer is every nation and tribe and tongue. John sees "…a multitude too large to count, from every nation and tribe and people and tongue…" (Revelation 7:9) That's a wide crowd, friends, from every direction. I'd need a lot more cookie boxes for it.

The answer is False. John says they "…were wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands." (Revelation 7:9) Sackcloth isn't mentioned anywhere in that picture, friends. It's white robes all around.

The answer is Lamb. The crowd cries out, "Salvation to our God, who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!" (Revelation 7:10) The Lamb is Jesus, the One John the Baptist pointed to when he said, "Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!" (John 1:29) The whole crowd says it together, friends, loud and clear.

The answer is that they fall facedown and worship God. The text says the angels "…fell facedown before the throne and worshiped God…" (Revelation 7:11) That's all the angels, friends, standing around the throne, the elders and the four living creatures. Then they start speaking their praise.

The answer is True. One of the elders asks John, "These in white robes, who are they, and where have they come from?" (Revelation 7:13) So the elder asks both who they are and where they came from, friends. The elder gives the answer a moment later.

The answer is the great tribulation. The elder says, "These are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation…" (Revelation 7:14) The text uses those words and gives no more detail, so we don't need to add any, friends. They came out of it, and now they stand before the throne.
The answer is the blood of the Lamb. The elder says, "they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb." (Revelation 7:14) That's the washing the verse names, friends.

The answer is False. The elder says, "Never again will they hunger, and never will they thirst; nor will the sun beat down upon them, nor any scorching heat." (Revelation 7:16) That's never again, friends, not just less. A promise like that is the best news I've heard in a while.

The answer is the Lamb in the center of the throne. The elder says, "…the Lamb in the center of the throne will be their shepherd." (Revelation 7:17) The Lamb is Jesus (John 1:29). Jesus also called Himself the good shepherd in John 10:11, friends, so it fits nicely.

The answers are water and tear. The elder says the Lamb "…will lead them to springs of living water…" (Revelation 7:17) That goes with the promise that they will never thirst. (Revelation 7:16) Then the elder says, "God will wipe away every tear from their eyes." (Revelation 7:17) Every tear, friends, not just most of them, and I think it's one of the kindest lines in the whole chapter.
